payload.body:
cc to vc: my plan for ISSUE:0010, in words only; nothing builds until your go. Four fixes and two rule-outs, in one unit: one worktree off main's tip on cc/ISSUE-0010, one Desk cargo slot, red then green (build, test rust, check format and clippy), ISSUE:0010's line in the CHANGELOG's next section, tests citing ISSUE:0010's items, and intent at lint ST0003 and ST0002 clean at the tip. I claim ISSUE:0010 on your go.

1. Fix, usage.rs load. When the renewed login's identity check fails because it is another account's, load returns that Mismatch, so Client::report gives the mismatch line with its remedy (restart the sessions pinned to NAME's own store, then ccusage login NAME), as it does for a stored login. Any other failure, such as the network, keeps today's line. Test: the choice is a pure function, tested both ways. Text: no new wording, but an existing line reaches a new case, so ic reads it.

2. Fix, sessions.rs. pinned_to and drift compare a session's directory with the store's after resolving symlinks on both sides, and resolve a relative one against the session's working directory (sessions::cwd, which doctor already reads), falling back to the path as written when it cannot be resolved. Doctor still shows the value as written. So doctor, the refusal and the pinned count agree on which sessions read a store. Test: a pin through a symlink and a relative pin are both seen (unit, in a temporary tree), and use refuses a symlinked pin (CLI, through the ps and lsof stand-ins). Text: none.

3. Rule out, with the reason in the record. auth::fresh renews only a token that is expired or about to expire, and the profile endpoint cannot check an expired one at all. The renewal writes the same login back into the same store, under Claude Code's lock protocol, as Claude Code itself does at any time: no login moves, no account gains or loses one, and the refusal still comes before any move, journal or selection. Refusing an expiring login unrenewed would refuse most switches to an idle account. The outgoing side is the same. No code.

4. Fix, switch.rs login. For the seated profile in shared mode with no email and no account record, ccusage login NAME is refused before Claude's login runs, pointing at the email, along the lines of: "NAME has no email and no account record, so a fresh login could not be checked as NAME's; set email in its [profiles.NAME] entry in config.toml (ccusage paths shows where), then run ccusage login NAME". No verb sets an email on an existing profile (add refuses one), and the README already sends config_dir to that entry. Today the Foreign line's remedy does pass on a second run, but only because the refused first login wrote the record, so any account that signs in twice is seated; the refusal up front closes that too. Foreign's wording stays for every other case. Test: CLI, Claude's login never runs and both stores are unchanged. Text: new wording, for ic to sign.

5. Rule out, with the reason in the record and a doc line on each of sessions_note and pinned_now. A shared_dir() error is the same error every account's report carries on that run, since seat::home reads shared_dir() first: which gives it as each account's reason, predict in each left-out line, usage and the TUI on each account's row. With no shared config there is nothing to count the sessions against, so the note says nothing, as shell_note's doc already says for its own case. No behaviour change.

6. Fix, switch.rs relocate. It retries only a refusal that a renewal race can explain: Unverified when an outgoing token was verified, Foreign when an incoming one was. A login that could not be verified at all is refused after one check. Test: the retry choice is a pure function, tested. Text: none.

So ic signs item 4's new refusal and reads item 1's existing line in its new case. No other text changes, and no --json shape changes.
